title: Rami son of Rav Yud
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He is mentioned in [Taanit 22b](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.22b.16): “Rami son of Rav Yud said: And in the Diaspora one sounds the alarm for it.” [Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Taanit.22b.15.1) explains: a sage whose name was Yud.

In [Pesachim 62b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.62b.15), Rami son of Rav Yuda says in the name of Rav: “From the day the Book of Genealogies was hidden away, the strength of the sages has weakened.” In [Zevachim 55b](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.55b.11), Rami son of Rav Yehudah cites Rav as saying, “There was a small opening,” etc. Hyman reports the reading Rav Yud in Dikdukei Soferim.[^2]

notes.text: Taanit 22b directly names Rami bar Rav Yud. The exact Dikdukei Soferim reading at Zevachim 55b has not been independently inspected; the Yud/Yuda/Yehudah forms remain as Hyman reports them.

The consulted texts give Yud in [Taanit 22b](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.22b.16), Yuda in [Pesachim 62b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.62b.15), and Yehudah in [Zevachim 55b](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.55b.11). Heilprin lists [the Taanit references under Yud](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3235&lang=en) and [the Pesachim and Zevachim references under Yuda](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3234&lang=en). Hyman’s reported apparatus reading remains a separate witness claim.
